overall: The AG found the Committee timely approved accurate November 2012 minutes, but violated the Law by failing to review a complaint before the Town Administrator responded to it; ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee failed to review her January 29, 2013 Open Meeting Law complaint before the Town Administrator responded for it.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not first review the complaint and authorize the Town Administrator to respond.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Committee did not approve its November 27, 2012 meeting minutes in a timely manner, waiting until May 1, 2013.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee meets only annually, the Committee may approve minutes at its next regularly scheduled meeting, even where that meeting is not for another year.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the draft minutes of the November 27, 2012 meeting were inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee substantially complied with the accuracy requirement, and that the minutes contain enough detail and accuracy so that a member of the public who did not attend the meeting could read the minutes and have a clear understanding of what occurred.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
